notes: These 9 Sigma rules detect FORANG/ARTEX's own operational fingerprints (defensive detection of the tool itself), not generic vulnerability classes. A hit on a finding means the finding's recorded evidence contains a string or behaviour the tool itself emits.

finding_classes is a heuristic keyword map (matched case-insensitively against the finding's vulnclass): it says which finding categories plausibly carry a rule's tokens in their evidence, not a semantic classification. Empty means the rule has no plausible class link and only matches evidence text.

The self-update rule pins forang-selfupdate: upstream pins artex-selfupdate, but FORANG renamed the string (selfupdate/github.go:98). The enrich UA, guard marker, CA filename and ports are unchanged from upstream and verified in FORANG source.
Correlation rules need a real event timeline (timestamps + group key); they are evaluated over recorded traffic events by rescan, not at finding registration time.

rules.description: Inbound HTTP requests whose User-Agent is artex-enrich/1.0, set by the FORANG asset-enrichment prober (enrich/enrich.go). Supporting indicator; an operator can change the User-Agent, so absence does not imply safety.
rules.title: FORANG Asset Enrichment Probe User-Agent

rules.description: Outbound User-Agent of the FORANG self-update routine. Upstream pins artex-selfupdate; FORANG renamed the string to forang-selfupdate (selfupdate/github.go:98), so this rule pins the FORANG value. Host/forensic egress indicator.
rules.title: FORANG Self-Update Egress User-Agent

rules.description: Platform-guard control marker written to the audit log on a blocked tool call (guard/guard.go). Host/forensic indicator; a single marker can also appear in a document that merely quotes it.
rules.title: FORANG Platform Guard Audit-Log Framing

rules.description: Destructive shell/DB commands mirroring the FORANG guard built-in deny list (db/db.go seed). Generic hunting lead, not a FORANG-specific signature; expect legitimate-administration matches. TRUNCATE is matched case-sensitively: the GNU coreutils truncate command shares the token and must not trip this rule.
rules.title: Destructive Command Execution (Guard-List Hunting)

rules.description: Creation of the recording proxy MITM CA file under the _ca/mitmproxy-ca-cert.pem layout (traffic/traffic.go). Both tokens must match: the bare filename alone is shared with standalone mitmproxy and does not trip this rule. Host/forensic artifact.
rules.title: FORANG Recording-Proxy MITM CA Certificate Artifact

rules.description: A burst of artex-enrich/1.0 probes from one source in a short window (enrichment runs at concurrency 4 with no rate limit). The velocity the single-request rule misses.
rules.title: FORANG Enrichment Scan Velocity (Burst From One Source)

rules.description: One source carrying the enrichment User-Agent to many distinct hosts: machine-speed fan-out across an asset list, where breadth (not just volume) is the tell.
rules.title: FORANG Enrichment Fan-Out (One Source, Many Distinct Hosts)

rules.description: Repeated platform-guard control markers on one host within a short window: an active FORANG run repeatedly tripping its guard, which removes the quote-a-marker false positive of the single event.
rules.title: FORANG Guard-Block Burst (Active Engaged Session)

rules.description: The guard marker and a destructive command co-occurring on one host within a window. Combining a FORANG-specific marker with the otherwise-generic destructive-command signal raises specificity.
rules.title: FORANG Guard Marker With Destructive Command on One Host

source: jiwoochris/artex-global detections/ (Sigma rules, ATT&CK layer, IoC CSV/MISP, Suricata rules, host triage), adapted for FORANG; retrieved 2026-11-27
